author: investopedia.com
title: Buy Bear Market Amazon: Nomura
text:
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) fell into correction territory on Monday amid a broader sell-off in the tech industry, leading some bulls on the Street to view the weakness as an opportunity to buy shares of the Seattle-based tech giant at a discount.
Amazon's Size and Scale 'Eclipsing its Ability to Suppress Margins' At Monday's close of $1,636.85, Amazon stock was down over 20% from its high of $2,050 reached in September, when the company briefly joined Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) as the only U.S. companies to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization. After closing down 4.4% on Monday, Amazon's total market cap fell to $809 billion, extending losses from late October, when Amazon offered December-quarter sales guidance well below the Street's forecasts.
In light of the sell-off, analysts at Nomura Instinet issued a note on Monday reiterating their buy rating on Amazon shares and predicting that profitability will rise significantly through fiscal 2022, as outlined by Barron's .
“AMZN’s size and scale are eclipsing its ability to suppress margins,” wrote Nomura analyst Simeon Siegel. “Put simply, it seems AMZN sales and GP [gross profit] dollars are growing faster than their ability to spend.”
Nomura is particularly upbeat on Amazon's leading public cloud platform Amazon Web Services (AWS) which accounted for a whopping 51% of profits in 2017, yet just 10% of total sales. Siegel also pointed to the burgeoning growth of Amazon's third-party sales business, which made up 53% of Amazon's unit sales volume as of the end of Q3.
"We believe the growth of AMZN’s marketplace has been and stands to be a powerful contributor to gross margin," said the analyst.
Trading up 1.4% on Tuesday morning at $1,659.62 Amazon stock reflects a 42% increase YTD, outperforming the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index's 5.5% increase and the S&P 500 index's 1.8% return over the same period.
According to CNBC , almost 73% of the technology sector is in correction territory, defined as a 10% or greater fall from a 52-week high, while 26 of 66 technology stocks in the S&P 500 are in bear market territory.
